_readme: DRAFTS FOR THE OWNER'S DONE-FLIP — [pipeline N-8 · N-9] Private/company/pipeline/06-app-build.md
🔴 THIS FILE IS NOT A DONE-RECORD AND NOTHING READS IT. `apps/subly/dod.json` is the record;
tooling/ci/assert-app-dod.mjs grades that file and knows nothing about this one (it reads a fixed
set of keys off a fixed path, so a sibling file is invisible to it). Every string below is an
UNSIGNED DRAFT written by an agent. A draft is a starting sentence with its evidence attached, so
the owner is answering a question rather than inventing one from a blank field. It is not a
verdict, and moving one of these strings into dod.json is an act only the owner performs.
WHY DRAFTS EXIST AT ALL. decisions-log 2026-08-09: "dod 13 strings: agent DRAFTS the 13 with
context; owner signs each before the atomic DONE flip (owner-voice rule intact)." The judgments
are his; the RECORDING of them is mechanical, and so is the legwork of measuring what he is being
asked to judge. Everything under `measured` in each row below was read off the tree at the commit
named in `draftedAgainst`, with file:line, not recalled.
WHAT THE 13 ARE, so the count is auditable rather than folklore:
N-8 → 4   the four humanReview VERDICTS (one per required row of tooling/dod-register.json's
`humanReviewRows`). These are judgments; nothing mechanical can produce them.
N-9 → 9   `selection`: record · sha256 · decided · decidedBy · gates.g1a · g1b · g1c · g2 · g3.
The gate answers are the owner's by requirement ("the gates are his"), and the record
they link lives in Private/company/, which no agent in the public worktree can write.
13        every field in dod.json that carries a JUDGMENT.
The record has 12 further blanks that `claiming-done` also refuses (reviewer · date · artifact, on
each of the four humanReview rows). They are NOT part of the 13 because none of them is a
judgment — a name, a calendar date, and the thing that was looked at. They are drafted anyway,
under `mechanicalCompanions`, so the flip is a copy rather than a scavenger hunt. 13 + 12 = 25 =
every blank in apps/subly/dod.json today.
🔴 THE FLIP IS ONE COMMIT OR NONE, AND THE 13 STRINGS ARE NOT SUFFICIENT ON THEIR OWN. Dropping
the exemption while the record still says `stamped` turns the lifecycle anchor red on the first
push (sites/_shared/_data/apps.json already advertises subly as "status": "live"), and flipping
the record to `claiming-done` while the exemption stands changes nothing at all, because an exempt
app is outside the guard's domain. `flipChecklist` below is the whole act in order, including one
thing that is neither a string nor a switch: a STALE MUTATION ROW that must be re-run first.
DELETE THIS FILE IN THE FLIP COMMIT. Its entire purpose is consumed the moment the strings land in
dod.json; a drafts file that outlives its flip is unsigned prose sitting next to a graded record,
reading like evidence. `flipChecklist` step 9 is that deletion.
NO BRICK TWIN, DELIBERATELY. The chassis rule is that a behavior in apps/subly is also a behavior in
tooling/bricks/app/__brick__ — but this is not a behavior, it is one app's homework for one owner act,
and it names subly's own screens at subly's own line numbers. A stamped app inheriting a file of
another app's measurements, pre-filled with verdicts nobody signed, is the exact failure the record
format exists to prevent. The BRICK's dod.json is the twin, and it already ships (with blanks).

ownerStrings.asks: loading (skeleton), empty (illustration+CTA), error (message+Retry) and offline are FOUR visually distinct outcomes on every data screen
measured: SIX data screens: home · calendar · insights · budget · detail · notifications.

home is the ONLY one that branches: lib/features/home/home_screen.dart:147 `.when(loading/error/data)`. Its loading arm is a bare CircularProgressIndicator (:151), not a skeleton; its error arm (:161) interpolates the raw exception into `couldNotLoad` and offers NO Retry control (the file's own comment at :154-160 records that leak as a known copy defect).

calendar:69 · insights:68 · budget:67 · detail:60 · notifications:22 each read `ref.watch(subscriptionsControllerProvider).valueOrNull ?? const []`. A FAILED fetch therefore renders as the empty state and is byte-indistinguishable from having no data.
budget_screen.dart:71 renders `Center(CircularProgressIndicator())` for the budget value with NO error branch at all.
No screen anywhere distinguishes OFFLINE from ERROR — there is no connectivity read in the app.
The two sheets are the exception and are proven: test/sheet_failure_surface_test.dart drives both failure paths, and both are feature rows in the record with watched mutations.
ownerStrings.draft: NOT HELD — 1 of 6 data screens distinguishes the states. home branches three ways (home_screen.dart:147) and even its error arm leaks the raw exception with no Retry; calendar, insights, budget, detail and notifications all read `.valueOrNull ?? const []`, so a failed fetch is rendered as the empty state and cannot be told apart from having no data; budget's own value is a bare spinner with no error branch; nothing anywhere distinguishes offline. The add and cancel sheets are the exception and are proven by sheet_failure_surface_test.dart. This is a known, priced gap, not a surprise: 39-CHASSIS §6 downgraded widget-per-state from CI precisely because seven screens x fifty apps of state widgets is unaffordable, and DoD item B stays `claim: "pending"` at the flip.
ownerStrings.signingThisMeans: Item B remains `"claim": "pending"` in dod.json after the flip. assert-app-dod.mjs permits that — for a `human` item, only `"held"` is constrained (it is refused while the app is `stamped`), so an app may claim done with a human item honestly pending. The alternative is to fix the five screens first and re-draft this row as a pass; that is a build decision, not a wording one.

ownerStrings.asks: first value arrives fast and the paywall sits AFTER the value moment. A judgment, never a threshold a guard may assert — the '60 seconds' in master-requirements §2.4 is a target with no measurement method
measured: THE ONLY GATED SURFACE is the Insights tab: lib/core/router.dart:229 `_GatedInsights` wraps it in the chassis `PaywallGate` (:235). Home, calendar, budget and settings are ungated. Nothing in the app forces a user onto /paywall.

🔴 THE GATE IS DORMANT TODAY. lib/state/money_providers.dart:168-174 — `paywallLockedProvider` returns false whenever `cfg.paywall.enabled` is false, and it is false in production. No user meets a wall right now.

FIRST VALUE SITS BEHIND A SIGN-IN. router.dart's redirect sends a signed-out user to /login for every location outside the auth flow (`/onboarding /login /sign-in /sign-up /scan`), so the dashboard is reached only after account creation. Onboarding runs FIRST and is exempt from the auth gate by design.
The flow is: /onboarding (3-step carousel) → /login → /home (the dashboard, which is the value moment) → Insights is behind it.
master-requirements §2.4's '60 seconds' has no measurement method; N-8 states explicitly that no guard may assert it.
ownerStrings.draft: HELD ON PLACEMENT, and the placement is currently unarmed. The one gated surface is the Insights tab (router.dart:229 `_GatedInsights` → PaywallGate); the dashboard, the renewal calendar and the budget are all reached without ever meeting a wall, so the value moment precedes the paywall rather than following it, and nothing forces /paywall on anybody. ⚠️ TWO FACTS THIS VERDICT RESTS ON, both of which change it if they change: (1) the gate is DORMANT — paywallLockedProvider returns false while paywall.enabled is false (money_providers.dart:168-174), so this is a judgment about a placement no user has met yet and it must be RE-SIGNED the day the enabled flip lands; (2) first value sits behind account creation — router.dart bounces a signed-out user to /login for everything outside the auth flow, so the 'fast' half is a sign-up cost, not a rendering cost. The 60-second figure is a target with no measurement method and is not being asserted here.
ownerStrings.signingThisMeans: This verdict expires by design at the paywall enabled-flip. That flip also arms the T-11 renewal-notice tripwire (legal K-13), and this row is dated, so once apps/subly/lib moves the staleness PRINT will name it on every run — printed, never failed ([pipeline C-6]).

ownerStrings.asks: the sha256 of that file, so a record edited after the decision cannot pass as the record that was decided
measured: check-selection-record.mjs:226 computes `createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(target)).digest('hex')` and compares with `!==` against this field — so it must be LOWERCASE hex of the file's raw bytes.
PowerShell's `Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 <path>` returns UPPERCASE. Lowercase it or the comparison fails with 'hashes to X, the done-record claims Y', which reads like tampering.
assert-app-dod.mjs cannot verify this at all and PRINTS 'not verifiable from the public repo' on every run — by design, so an unperformed check never looks like a performed one.
ownerStrings.draft: <64 lowercase hex chars — compute AFTER the record file is final>
ownerStrings.signingThisMeans: Compute it last, from the finished file: `(Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 company/app-selection/subly.md).Hash.ToLower()`. Any later edit to that file — even a typo fix — invalidates this string and must be followed by re-hashing and a new commit. That expiry is the point of the field.

ownerStrings.asks: Zero-freshness — 'content stays valid ≥12 months (no prices, news, tax rates) or generate-once breaks' (master-requirements §2.1)
measured: Subly ships NO pre-generated content pack. There is no packs directory, no bundled corpus, and no R2-served content in the app — its data is the user's own subscription entries, created at runtime.
The gate exists to protect the margin thesis (§1.1: generate once, COGS ≈ $0). An app with nothing generated has nothing that can go stale.

What DOES age is the surrounding copy, not content: currency formatting, the store listing and the legal pages. None of those is what G2 measures, and each has its own owner (stage 10, the legal tripwires).

⚠️ Subly is the rail-prover, not a catalogue app. When the first content-pack app (Lingo, Tales, Decks) reaches this gate, this answer will NOT transfer and must be argued from the pack's own shelf life.
ownerStrings.draft: PASS, and trivially so, for the reason that makes it uninformative for every later app: Subly ships no pre-generated content at all. There is no content pack, no bundled corpus and no R2-served data — the subscriptions are the user's own entries, created at runtime — so there is nothing that can be twelve months stale. The user-visible copy (currency formatting, store listing, legal pages) does age, but that is not what this gate measures and each of those has its own owner. This answer is worth nothing to the first content-pack app and must be argued there from that pack's shelf life.
ownerStrings.signingThisMeans: Recording a trivially-passed gate as trivially passed, rather than as a pass. A gate that reads 'PASS' with no reason attached is the shape that gets copied into an app where it is false.

ownerStrings.asks: Do-no-harm — 'wrong content can't hurt anyone (no medical dosing, foraging, etc., without expert review)' (master-requirements §2.1)

The realistic harm surface is FINANCIAL-ADJACENT, not physical: a wrong renewal date, or a cancel flow that claims success when it failed. The second is guarded — cancel_sheet.dart:_confirm's failure path is a feature row proved by a watched mutation, and the test is named 'cancel sheet: a failed cancel never claims success'.
The app does not touch the user's money: no bank connection, no card, and the purchase rail is dormant (paywall.enabled false).
Deletion fails CLOSED and says so rather than half-erasing (services/*/src/routes/account.ts) — that posture was live-proven the hard way on 2026-08-09.
ownerStrings.draft: PASS. There is no health, safety, legal or navigational content anywhere in the app — it displays the user's own entries and arithmetic over them. The realistic harm surface is financial-adjacent rather than physical, and both halves of it are addressed rather than assumed: a cancel that fails never shows the congratulation step (cancel_sheet.dart:_confirm, proved by a watched mutation whose test is named 'a failed cancel never claims success'), and the app connects to no bank and holds no card, so a wrong number here misinforms a decision but cannot move money. The one thing it could get wrong in a way a user would act on is a renewal date, which is derived arithmetic over data the user entered and can see.
ownerStrings.signingThisMeans: You are signing that the failure modes are informational. If a future release ever moves money, cancels a real service on the user's behalf, or ingests financial accounts, this gate is re-opened — none of those is true today.

_why: assert-app-dod.mjs refuses `claiming-done` while ANY of verdict/reviewer/date/artifact is blank on ANY
of the four humanReview rows. These twelve are therefore required by the flip, but none of them is one
of the 13: a name, a date and the thing that was looked at are records, not judgments. Drafted here so

reviewer.note: N-8's four judgments are one sign-off event, not four ceremonies — the same reviewer on all four rows is the intended shape.

date.note: The day you actually review, YYYY-MM-DD, not in the future. ⚠️ apps/subly/lib last changed 2026-08-10 (UTC) — it said 2026-08-09 here until the 2026-08-10 re-run measured it again, which is the same one-day drift that expired seven mutation rows — so the 2026-08-09 draft above is ALREADY one day stale and prints for all four rows; MEASURED in the flip preflight: 'humanReview "polish" was signed 2026-08-09; apps/subly/lib last changed 2026-08-10', ×4. Write the day you actually review. A date EARLIER than lib's last change makes assert-app-dod.mjs print a staleness line for the row on every run — printed, never failed ([pipeline C-6]: a guard on owner-gated work must not halt CI). Every later commit under apps/subly/lib re-arms that print, which is the design: a human verdict is a state that ages, not an event. ⚠️ AND WRITE THE UTC DAY, not the IST one: the guard compares this string against a UTC `today` and a UTC-normalised git commit day, and between 00:00 and 05:30 IST those are yesterday's date — the recorded scar that reddened four fixtures on 2026-08-03.

artifact.note: N-8's replacement acceptance #2: 'a commit SHA or a screenshot path. A verdict with no artifact is a memory.' Replace 255265b with the sha you actually looked at, and if you reviewed screenshots rather than the live site, name the paths instead. The four rows may legitimately carry different artifacts — the polish row is the one most likely to want screenshots (splash and loading states), since those are the limbs it fails on.

flipChecklist: 🔴 ONE COMMIT OR NONE. Steps 2 and 3 in isolation each produce a WRONG state: dropping the exemption alone turns the lifecycle anchor red on the first push (sites/_shared/_data/apps.json already says "status": "live", and a live app whose record says `stamped` FAILS — that is the anchor working); flipping the record alone changes nothing at all, because an exempt app is outside the guard's domain.

1 · ✅ DONE 2026-08-10 (UTC) — AND IT WAS SEVEN ROWS, NOT ONE. As drafted, this step named `edit profile` alone and closed with 'Measured 2026-08-09: this is the ONLY stale row of the fourteen'. That was true when measured and false by the time this file merged: the auth/router work of 2026-08-09..10 moved six files under apps/subly/lib, and every row anchored to one of them expired together — sign out · finish onboarding · edit profile · consent prompt · dark mode · home · budget. Running the guard with the exemption removed printed all seven, so the count was never a judgement call.
